solutionSql:
WITH first_booking AS (
  SELECT customer_id,
         DATE_TRUNC('month', (MIN(booked_at) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')) AS cohort_month
  FROM shipments
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT TO_CHAR(f.cohort_month, 'YYYY-MM') AS cohort,
       COUNT(*)::integer AS cohort_size,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (
         WHERE EXISTS (
           SELECT 1
           FROM shipments s
           WHERE s.customer_id = f.customer_id
             AND DATE_TRUNC('month', (s.booked_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')) = f.cohort_month + INTERVAL '1 month'
         )
       )::integer AS retained
FROM first_booking f
GROUP BY f.cohort_month
ORDER BY f.cohort_month;

rules.howSolved: The first_booking CTE holds one row per customer, so cohort_size counts only customers whose first UTC booking fell in that month.
Retention is an EXISTS test per customer in first_booking, so a customer who booked several times is counted at most once.
EXISTS checks for a shipment whose UTC month equals cohort_month + 1 month, which also handles the December to January wrap.

notes: Cohort month uses timezone(UTC) on MIN(booked_at). Ran without error on sample, nulls and boundary. The sample has one cohort (2025-12, 6 customers) and all 6 are retained, so the sample cannot tell next-month retention apart from ever-returning logic; the hidden datasets carry that check. Session TimeZone is UTC, and the sample has no month-boundary rows where session and UTC months differ.
